subtopics.title: Why Four Terms Demand a Different Tool

questions.question: In factorisation, what does a count of FOUR terms signal?
options: The difference of squares
Factorising by grouping in pairs
The trinomial product-and-sum method
The expression cannot be factorised

questions.question: Why is there no overall common factor in 3mp + 3mq − np − nq?
options: Because the expression has too many terms
Because 3 divides every term
The first two terms carry m and no n, the last two carry n and no m, and no number beyond 1 divides all four
Because p and q appear in every term

questions.question: What LOCAL structure makes grouping possible in 3mp + 3mq − np − nq?
options: Each pair of terms shares its own common factor even though all four share nothing
All four terms are perfect squares
The terms alternate in sign
The expression is secretly a trinomial

subtopics.title: Factoring Each Pair — and the Negative Factor Trap

questions.question: Factoring 3m out of 3mp + 3mq leaves:
options: (mp + mq)
(p + q)
(3m + pq)

questions.question: Factoring POSITIVE n out of −np − nq creates a problem because:
options: n cannot divide into np
The result n(−p − q) has a bracket that does not match the first pair's (p + q)
The result equals zero
Positive factors are never allowed

questions.question: The rule for a pair that BEGINS with a minus sign is:
options: Erase the minus signs inside the bracket
Swap the two terms first
Skip that pair and factor the other one twice
Factor out a NEGATIVE common factor so the signs inside flip into agreement

questions.question: Dividing −np by −n gives:
options: +p, because a minus divided by a minus is a plus
−p
−np²
+n

subtopics.title: The Common Bracket — Finishing the Factorisation

questions.question: 3m(p + q) − n(p + q) factorises fully to:
options: (p + q)(p − q)
3m − n(p + q)

questions.question: What does a MISMATCH between the two brackets tell you?
options: The expression is prime
Something upstream is wrong — usually a positive factor where a negative belonged, or a pairing that needs rearranging
You should multiply the brackets together anyway
The answer is the mismatched brackets side by side

questions.question: The four terms 3mp − nq − np + 3mq refuse to pair as given. The correct fix is:
options: Declare the expression unfactorisable
Change the minus signs to plus signs
Rearrange the terms so kin sits with kin: 3mp + 3mq − np − nq, then group as usual
Divide every term by p

questions.question: How do you PROVE that (p + q)(3m − n) is the correct factorisation?
options: Substitute p = q = 0 only
Compare it with the difference of squares
Check that the brackets look symmetrical
Expand it and confirm all four original terms return with their correct signs

subtopics.title: The Full Method, the Checks, and Where Grouping Hides

questions.question: The five-step grouping method opens with:
options: Checking for an overall common factor
Splitting the middle term
Expanding all brackets
Equating the expression to zero

questions.question: In 2cd + 6c − d − 3, the second pair −d − 3 is factored as:
options: −1(d + 3), using minus one as the negative common factor

questions.question: Stopping at 3m(p + q) − n(p + q) loses marks because:
options: The brackets should have been expanded
The expression should first have been divided by p + q
It is only a rest stop — the shared bracket must still be factored out to finish
The minus sign should be removed

questions.question: Where does grouping reappear inside OTHER techniques?
options: It finishes the trinomial method after the middle term is split, and completes cubic factorisations later on
It never reappears — it is a standalone trick
Only in geometry problems
Only when an expression has exactly two terms

subtopics.title: Sorting the Shopping Into Two Bags

questions.question: The 'two bags' in the shopping picture stand for:
options: The two pairs of terms, each sharing its own common factor
The two sides of an equation
The numerator and denominator
Positive and negative numbers

questions.question: After lifting 3m out of the first bag, the bracket holds (p + q) because:
options: p and q are the largest terms
brackets always hold the smallest letters
A bracket carries the LEFTOVERS — the parts the two terms did not share
p and q were shared by both terms

questions.question: Which term count calls for which tool?
options: Two terms: grouping; three: identities; four: trinomial method
Two terms: squares or cubes identities; three: product-and-sum hunt; four: grouping in pairs
The count never matters
Four terms: difference of squares

subtopics.title: The Minus That Must Come Out

questions.question: Lifting positive n out of −np − nq gives n(−p − q). Why is this a dead end?
options: The bracket (−p − q) is not a twin of the first bag's (p + q), and the next move needs identical brackets
Because n is too small a factor
Because brackets may never contain minus signs
It is not a dead end — the answer is finished

questions.question: Lifting NEGATIVE n out of −np − nq gives:
options: n(p + q)
−n(p + q), because dividing by a negative flips the signs inside
−n(p − q)

questions.question: Why may you NOT simply erase the minus signs inside a bracket to force a match?
options: Because erasing changes the value of the expression — the insides may only change if the factor outside changes to pay for it
Because examiners prefer minus signs
You may — it is a standard shortcut
Because brackets are permanent once written

subtopics.title: The Same Bracket in Both Hands

questions.question: Nicknaming the bracket (p + q) as B turns 3mB − nB into:
options: B(3m − n) — the bracket comes out like any other factor
3mn − B
B²(3m − n)
(3m − n) with B discarded

questions.question: The matching bracket acts as a free error alarm because:
options: Brackets always match in correct maths
Twin brackets confirm the sorting and signs were right; different brackets signal an upstream error to fix, never to force
It counts the number of terms for you
It removes the need for any checking

questions.question: A four-term expression whose given order refuses to pair is usually:
options: Prime
A trick question with no answer
A seating problem — reshuffle so family sits with family, then group as normal
Solvable only by the quadratic formula

questions.question: Expanding (p + q)(3m − n) returns:
options: 3mp + 3mq − np − nq — all four original terms with their signs
3mp − 3mq + np − nq
3m²p²q²
p + q + 3m − n
